Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 1. Platform Overview

Picom365 is ScImage's flagship cloud-based imaging platform, used across
radiology, cardiology, vascular medicine, women's health, and several other
clinical specialties. It's built as a suite of interconnected web applications
and modules rather than a single monolithic app, all accessed through a
common login portal at picom365.com.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. High-Level Workflow

At a high level, an exam or study moves through the platform in five stages:

● Acquisition & Upload — Images/exams enter the system from

modalities, mobile capture, or web upload.
● Worklist & Routing — Studies are organized, prioritized, and routed to

the right reader.
● Viewing & Diagnosis — Clinicians review images using

specialty-specific viewers and tools.
● Reporting — Findings are documented, either through built-in or

external reporting systems.
● Distribution, Sharing & Analytics — Results and images are shared

with referring providers/patients, and usage/outcomes data is tracked
centrally.

Administration (user accounts, permissions) and interoperability with
outside systems (EHRs, other PACS, HL7 feeds) run underneath all five
stages rather than as a separate step.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. High-Level Workflow > 2.1 Acquisition & Upload

● PicomCloud — a web-based upload portal for submitting patient

exams directly, without needing local PACS infrastructure.
● PicomCam — a mobile app that lets staff capture photos on a

phone/tablet and upload them straight into the PACS, used heavily in
specialties like wound care, dermatology, or endoscopy where
photographic documentation matters.
● Modality-originated studies (CT, MRI, ultrasound, echo, etc.) flow in

through standard DICOM and non-DICOM ingestion, since the
platform is built to handle both.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. High-Level Workflow > 2.2 Worklist & Routing

● A smart worklist dynamically prioritizes urgent cases (STAT/ASAP) and auto-routes

studies by modality, subspecialty, or site.
● Automated alerts notify assigned readers of time-sensitive studies, with per-user tracking

configurable down to the hour or minute.
● A built-in patient/study identifier crosswalk lets the system reconcile records across

multiple EHRs or multiple radiology groups serving one institution, which matters for
multi-site or multi-tenant deployments.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. High-Level Workflow > 2.3 Viewing & Diagnosis

Viewing is delivered through specialty-tuned dashboards under the shared
PicomWeb front end, rather than one generic viewer:

● Radiology — zero-footprint 2D/3D viewing, AI-assisted hanging

protocols and prior-study surfacing, MPR/MIP and image fusion, and
integration hooks into external advanced-visualization/quantification
tools.
● Cardiology — workflows spanning invasive and diagnostic cardiology.
● Vascular — support for both invasive and non-invasive vascular

imaging workflows.
● Women's Health — dedicated handling for OB, MFM (maternal-fetal

medicine), and mammography studies.

● Other departments — ophthalmology, endoscopy, dermatology, and

pathology are supported through the same underlying platform.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. High-Level Workflow > 2.4 Reporting

● Structured Reporting — configurable templates for generating

standardized reports, aimed at specialties with data-rich exam types
(e.g., cardiology).
● Voice-enabled self-reporting, using built-in speech recognition, for

dictation directly inside the platform.
● External reporting integration — the platform can either launch a

third-party reporting system from within PACS, or be launched/driven
from an external system, so sites aren't locked into one reporting tool.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. High-Level Workflow > 2.5 Distribution, Sharing & Analytics

● PicomShare — lets external physicians and patients submit or

receive exams, functioning as the platform's exam-exchange front
door.
● Secure image sharing — web-link-based, PHI-protected distribution

intended to replace physical media (CDs), aimed at cutting
unnecessary re-imaging, radiation exposure, turnaround time, and
cost.
● PicomAnalytics — a reporting/analytics module for tracking worker

productivity and patient-outcome data across the organization.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. High-Level Workflow > 2.6 Cross-Cutting: Administration

● AdminConsole — centralized control over user accounts and access

permissions, used to configure who can see or do what across the
platform.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. High-Level Workflow > 2.7 Cross-Cutting: Interoperability

Underneath the specialty workflows sits what ScImage calls the
Interoperability Core, which handles:

● HL7, EHR, DICOM, and non-DICOM data exchange
● Billing and patient-ID reconciliation across systems
● Connections to legacy EHRs, external reporting systems, VNAs

(vendor-neutral archives), and third-party PACS
● Support for flexible exchange patterns: subspecialty reading,

teleradiology, consolidated worklists, and HIE/MPI (health information
exchange/master patient index) translation

This is the layer that lets a single radiology group serve multiple institutions
with different EHRs, or multiple groups serve one institution, without
manual reconciliation.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 4. Sourcing Notes

This overview reflects publicly available descriptions from picom365.com
and scimage.com as of September 2026, and is a paraphrased summary of
ScImage's own marketing content — not verbatim reproduction. It

describes the platform ScImage has built and operates; it does not describe
or imply any Tecsack ownership of Picom365 as a whole. Documenting
Tecsack's specific contracted contribution to this platform is a separate,
distinctly scoped piece of work.
